name: Scar of the Worldbreaker
summary: The Scar of the Worldbreaker is a dramatic geographic scar cutting through the rugged terrain of the Badlands. Associated with deep earth tremors and the ancient, terrifying legacy of the black dragon Deathwing, it is a stark reminder of primordial destructive forces.

sections.title: A Rift in the Badlands
sections.body: Running through the arid reaches of the western Badlands, this rent in the stone stands apart from the natural dry canyons of the desert. The scorched and shattered stone bears all the hallmarks of violent draconic power, whispered by seasoned explorers to be tied to the Earth-Warder turned Worldbreaker, Deathwing. The sheer devastation cuts near old pathways, leaving the earth broken and scorched.

sections.title: Lingering Destruction
sections.body: Surrounding regions such as the Dustbowl and the Mirage Flats show the lingering impact of seismic and fiery upheavals. The raw, jagged stone and molten remnants throughout the area serve as a grim testament to the catastrophic power of the Black Aspect, whose shadow has scarred Azeroth's landscape for generations.

faq.q: What is the Scar of the Worldbreaker?
faq.answer: It is a massive, charred furrow cut deeply into the stone of the western Badlands, bearing marks of immense heat and violence.

faq.q: Why is it called the Scar of the Worldbreaker?
faq.answer: The moniker refers to Deathwing, the corrupted Black Dragon Aspect once known as Neltharion the Earth-Warder, whose immense earth-shattering power is credited with carving the rift.
No. The rift is a mark of past devastation and earth-shattering power, though the Black Dragonflight's brood and lingering corruption still haunt various corners of the world.
The scar cuts near Angor Fortress and divides portions of the arid plains, impacting areas stretching toward the Dustbowl, Camp Wurg, and the Mirage Flats.

angles.text: The tortured, melted stone here screams of elements torn and twisted by unnatural violence rather than the peaceful will of the earth spirits.
The sheared rock faces and exposed deep strata reveal scorched minerals and heavy stones dredged up from deep beneath the surface.
